claude_code_trading_bot_handoff.purpose: Give Frank's EXISTING day-trading bot a clear operating environment and direct Claude Code to improve that bot. This is an actionable implementation prompt to use together with Trading-bot-code-master.pdf, not a replacement strategy or a request for a 340-section essay. The finished goal is a validated, fully autonomous personal-live bot. The immediate goal is a working, measurable, autonomous paper-trading path in the existing project.

document.instruction: Read all 20 pages before changing the bot. Frank will supply this PDF in the same Claude Code session or make it accessible in the project. Its reconciled strategy, safety, risk, stage definitions, proposed pilot defaults, tests, and promotion gates are the detailed implementation requirements. If the PDF is unavailable or unreadable, report that specific dependency and inspect the existing project; do not invent its contents or claim implementation is complete.

Inspect the repository, project instructions, configuration, existing audit findings, working risk engine, kill switch, simulator, ledger, data providers, strategy code, tests, and any uncommitted work. Confirm audit claims against the actual checkout. Preserve working behavior and record discrepancies before making bounded edits.

authority_and_change_control.rule: Frank's latest explicit instruction governs his intent and requested scope.
Respect applicable project instructions and hard safety or authorization boundaries.

Use the approved master PDF for detailed implementation. This XML defines how to use it, the operating stages, and a bounded research environment. It does not silently override PDF strategy rules, risk limits, or promotion gates.

Where working repository behavior conflicts with the PDF, inspect the evidence, preserve sound components, implement the PDF's intended behavior in a versioned way, and document the change. Where a material ambiguity cannot be resolved from the PDF, implement independent work and mark only the dependent feature unresolved.
Do not treat the older research-only XML prompt, its prefilled response, or its list of 340 report sections as a second instruction set. This file supersedes that prompt.

The XML is a prompt and design reference. It is not an executable strategy or broker configuration. Translate chosen rules into typed, versioned repository configuration with validated units, defaults, and tests.
Record strategy, data, account-rule, cost-model, and code versions. Never silently alter thresholds or relabel past evidence after a material rule change.

authorization.allowed_now: Inspect the existing project; make bounded, reversible code and configuration changes needed for the approved autonomous paper path; add the defined strategy and risk tests; run development tests, synthetic replay, and genuine paper sessions when data and time permit; build manual prop alerts and rule interfaces without order access.
authorization.not_authorized_now: Place any real-money order; send, prefill, modify, or cancel an order in the prop account; connect a prop execution route; activate autonomous personal-live trading; use protected final out-of-sample data before its planned release; self-modify a live model or risk parameter; buy or reset a prop account; or expand into new markets or strategy families by default.
authorization.scope_rule: A change to this prompt is not an authorization to cross an operating-stage boundary. Promotion requires the evidence and explicit activation specified in the master PDF.

owner_intent_and_evidence.goal: Build a day-trading bot targeting at least 70 percent wins; 75 percent is a higher objective.
owner_intent_and_evidence.source_engine: Frank reports that the photographed Quant Farming guide summarizes a separate, successful live signal engine at about 70 percent wins. Treat this as a user-attested source-engine benchmark and a source of candidate parameters. It is not the measured win rate of Frank's bot and is not a trade-level ledger supplied with this handoff.
owner_intent_and_evidence.current_bot: The revised audit supplied to the master on 29 September 2026 describes Frank's actual bot and updates his size, risk, exit, and session answers. It still reports no completed strategy paper trades at that point, so the bot's own out-of-sample win rate and net expectancy are unknown. Verify the current checkout rather than assuming the audit is a live view of every file.
owner_intent_and_evidence.evidence_labels: Always distinguish SOURCE_ENGINE_REPORT, SYNTHETIC_TEST, HISTORICAL_DEVELOPMENT, WALK_FORWARD, PROTECTED_OOS, AUTONOMOUS_PAPER, MANUAL_PROP, and PERSONAL_LIVE. Do not pool these ledgers or imply that a target has been demonstrated.

operating_modes.mode: The deterministic bot detects setups, checks data and risk, sizes integer contracts, enters and exits through a simulator, manages protective state, and records results. No real trading adapter or real account credentials are reachable from this mode.

The bot analyzes and recommends entry, management, and exit actions. Frank personally reviews, enters, protects, modifies, and closes each prop order. Bot alerts cannot submit, prefill, modify, or cancel prop orders or operate the trading interface. Record Frank's actual actions separately from paper fills. Activate only with the selected account's current rule profile and tested route isolation.

Future autonomous execution is for a permitted personal broker account after all promotion requirements, broker-adapter qualification, and Frank's explicit activation. Merely implementing an adapter must not enable this mode.
operating_modes.stage_order: PAPER_AUTO to PROP_MANUAL_ALERTS to separately authorized LIVE_AUTO.

active_paper_strategy.instruction: Preserve the existing multi-timeframe liquidity strategy described in the master. Use sound, already-tested repository definitions when equivalent. Where a definition is missing, use the master's explicitly labeled paper-pilot interpretation in a separately versioned variant. Do not claim proposed values came from the source engine.
active_paper_strategy.pilot_instrument: MES first; retain other requested markets as future research candidates.
active_paper_strategy.revised_session: The revised audit permits trading after the market opens and forbids premarket entries. Proposed MES paper window: 09:30-11:30 America/New_York, flat by 11:30. The US equity cash open is 09:30 ET, not the form's stated 09:00. Wait for the required completed bar, valid quote, event and regime checks; do not force an entry at the opening print. The old first-30-minute exclusion no longer applies.
active_paper_strategy.timeframes: H4 and H1 for aligned bias and liquidity context; M15 and M5 for setup confirmation; M1 for entry confirmation. Use completed bars and known-at-decision timestamps.
active_paper_strategy.setup: Implement the master's aligned-bias, premarked liquidity, sweep and rejection, displacement, structural confirmation, M1 retest, structural stop, and directional liquidity target as one separately tagged setup.

Implement the master's aligned-bias, unconsumed target, M5 displacement and aligned gap, qualifying pullback, M1 respect and confirmation, structural stop, and target as a separate setup. Do not impose a reversal sweep on every continuation trade.
active_paper_strategy.no_trade_rule: Missing confirmation, stale data, unknown contract metadata, insufficient risk capacity, a consumed target, poor executable price, invalid payoff, or an account-rule block produces a recorded skip. Distinguish a valid no-setup session from a broken pipeline.
active_paper_strategy.accumulation_state: Implement the master's proposed accumulation/compression candidate as a causal market state. Use a frozen prior M5 range and completed-bar efficiency and ATR measurements. Price compression is not proof of institutional buying. Record range and transition states, false breaks, skipped interior crossovers, and unknown data. REVERSAL_R1 still needs its complete boundary-sweep setup; CONTINUATION_C1 still needs its full breakout and pullback confirmation. Keep moving-average slope and low-liquidity diagnostics versioned and test their incremental value before adding new numeric gates.

research_environment.purpose: Preserve the useful ideas from Frank's original XML as testable context. They are candidates for diagnostic features or separately versioned strategy variants. They do not automatically become entry gates, change the baseline, or create a claim of incremental edge.
research_environment.candidate_market_structure: Define and test support, resistance, supply, demand, displacement, gaps, fair-value gaps, zone freshness, mitigation, failed breaks, sweeps, and actual follow-through from information available at the decision time. Price reactions may identify a candidate liquidity level; they do not prove resting orders or replenishment without appropriate order-book or trade evidence. Test whether repeated touches strengthen or consume a level rather than assuming either result.
research_environment.candidate_accumulation_evidence: Compare observable compression with preceding trend, valid contract volume, and order-flow data only when actually available. Distinguish accumulation, reaccumulation, distribution, and generic range as research labels; do not infer hidden inventory or future breakout direction from price alone.
research_environment.candidate_timeframe_variant: Research H4 trend, M30 structure, M15 location, and M5 entry as an alternative to the active H4/H1/M15/M5/M1 hierarchy. A countertrend mean-reversion setup must be a separate research variant; it must not bypass the active aligned-bias rule. Compare each hierarchy against a simpler baseline using causal, completed bars.
research_environment.candidate_indicators: Study RSI as a measured momentum feature, with 14 as a research baseline and 5, 7, 9, 21, and 28 as controlled alternatives. Specify smoothing, warm-up, zero-gain/loss handling, and timestamps. Overbought does not itself mean short; oversold does not itself mean long. Test slope, divergence, and thresholds only for value beyond price, trend, volatility, and other correlated measures. Study mathematical moving-average slope and normalized price distance. VIX is conditional context when causally available and useful; no automatic inverse direction rule applies.
research_environment.candidate_mean_reversion: Define the mean or equilibrium, its anchor and update policy, regime, extension, supply or demand response, entry, invalidation, stop, target, time horizon, and no-hit outcome before testing. VWAP, anchored VWAP, rolling mean, median, range midpoint, and point of control are alternative references, not interchangeable numerical meanings. Test supply-to-mean shorts and demand-to-mean longs separately. A gap need not fill and a price need not return to its mean.
research_environment.candidate_breakout: Define boundary, close, displacement, acceptance, follow-through, optional retest, expiration, and execution time. Distinguish valid breakout, failed breakout, false breakout, and sweep without using later candles to justify an earlier fill. Test quick spikes as separate continuation and exhaustion hypotheses.
research_environment.candidate_regime_and_confluence: Quantify bull, bear, range, chop, and transition using completed data. Compare hard gates with simple scores and calibrated models. Do not count RSI, momentum, moving-average slope, and recent returns as independent votes when they encode the same move. More confluence does not automatically raise win probability.
research_environment.candidate_execution: Compare market, limit, marketable-limit, stop, and stop-limit policies under measured spread, fill probability, latency, adverse selection, and missed fills. Initial paper fills must follow the master simulator policy. A diagnostic ablation without costs cannot qualify a deployable strategy.
research_environment.research_order: Form an operational definition; name its observable data and availability time; register a hypothesis and simpler comparator; test on development data; run chronological walk-forward and feature ablations; evaluate net results after execution costs; record failure and uncertainty; promote only by a documented new version and forward evidence. Do not force a 340-section written report.

instrument_and_data_environment.universe: Retain Frank's stated research list: US 30, VIX, NAS1, VXI, XAUL, ES, and MES. The old XML also suggested NQ; treat NQ as an unapproved expansion candidate. Do not equate aliases with exchange contracts without mapping provider, venue, symbol, contract month, multiplier, tick size/value, expiry, and session.
instrument_and_data_environment.vix_rule: Distinguish the spot VIX index used as context from an actual tradable volatility product. Use VIX only when its feed, timestamp, and market relevance are known.
instrument_and_data_environment.futures_rule: Futures expire or settle. Record the actual contract and a causal rollover policy. A continuous research series is not an executable contract. Treat ES and MES as correlated exposure rather than independent opportunities.
instrument_and_data_environment.data_rule: Keep exchange, receive, bar-close, and decision timestamps; session timezone, daylight-saving policy, holidays, maintenance windows, quote validity, bid/ask, contract roll, data gaps, and data-source version. Use only data available before each decision. Historical OHLC bars alone cannot validate queue fills or live spread.
instrument_and_data_environment.event_rule: Scheduled news is a risk, volatility, and liquidity filter; do not infer direction from an announcement. Apply the master's proposed blackout and flattening policy in paper mode unless a stricter existing rule applies. Missing required calendar data blocks new entries while protective handling continues.

risk_and_order_invariants.budget: Implement the master's paper defaults and any stricter existing safeguards: synthetic starting equity 50000 USD, static synthetic floor 48500 USD, execution reserve 100 USD, maximum new-trade dollar cap 100 USD, five percent of remaining usable loss capacity as the capacity cap, net daily stop 150 USD, and one MES contract maximum. These are proposed PAPER settings, not a selected prop firm's rules. With initial usable capacity 1400 USD, the capacity cap is 70 USD. Recompute against active exposure, pending reservations, account floor, daily headroom, and other limits before each entry. The revised audit states 0.25-0.5 percent of nominal trading capital per trade, 1 percent nominal daily loss, and 25 percent of the allowed drawdown per day as Frank's upper internal ceilings. At 50000 USD, these correspond to 125-250 USD trade risk, 500 USD daily loss, and 375 USD of the synthetic 1500 USD drawdown allowance. The stricter 70 USD initial capacity budget and 150 USD paper daily stop control the pilot. Do not treat these user ceilings as a current prop firm's rules.
risk_and_order_invariants.sizing: stop_ticks = abs(entry_price - stop_price) / tick_size. unit_loss = stop_ticks * tick_value + round_trip_cost + stressed_slippage. affordable_quantity = floor(available_trade_budget / unit_loss). approved_quantity = minimum of affordable_quantity and all instrument, internal, account, and margin caps. Round prices to valid ticks without understating loss. If quantity is zero, skip; never move the structural stop merely to fit the budget. Reserve capacity atomically before order submission. The old XML's approximate one-percent-of-equity ceiling is a research scenario, not an active replacement for this capacity-based pilot. The revised one-to-three-micro answer is a maximum range, not a requirement to hold at least one contract. The pilot remains one MES; any later three-micro cap needs a separately validated profile and all dollar-risk checks.
risk_and_order_invariants.payoff_and_expectancy: Use the master's proposed minimum gross target-to-stop ratio of 1.0 for the initial paper variant, then measure realized net results. A 70 to 75 percent win rate alone cannot pass a strategy if average winners, losers, and costs produce negative net expectancy. Planning assumptions such as p = 0.65 may support initial paper decisions only if labeled as assumptions. Do not claim calibrated probabilities before the required evidence exists.
risk_and_order_invariants.exits: Frank's revised ordinary exit is at the stop or take-profit. The master's 30-minute maximum hold and event/session flattening are additional proposed protective exits for paper trading. Record each exit reason distinctly and test the effect before changing the policy. Do not imply those time exits were specified in Frank's revised answer.
risk_and_order_invariants.hard_rules: No martingale, averaging into losses, automatic geometric size escalation, backward stop widening, or changing the stop to avoid a loss. Do not start a new entry after the master's daily dollar stop, three-entry session cap, or three-consecutive-loss pause triggers. Existing protective management continues through pauses, stale data, disconnection, and entry lockout.
risk_and_order_invariants.execution_sequence: Validate market and account state; detect a causal setup; choose entry, invalidation, stop, and target; estimate executable price and costs; check payoff, assumed or measured expectancy, and uncertainty; size whole contracts; enforce every risk and account rule; reserve capacity; authorize the mode-specific action; submit a simulated order or emit a manual alert; reconcile fills and protection; manage the position; record the final outcome. Execution feasibility analysis may precede risk approval; an actual order cannot.

probability_and_decision_semantics.outcomes: For a fixed setup, entry, stop, target, and time horizon, define mutually exclusive target-first, stop-first, time-exit, no-fill, and relevant partial-fill outcomes. Resolve both-levels-touched bars with finer data or a conservative documented policy. Mean-hit and breakout labels can overlap these outcomes; do not sum overlapping probabilities as if disjoint.
probability_and_decision_semantics.estimation: Use explicit NOT_ESTIMATED or null values when a probability or model score is unavailable. A confluence score is not a probability. Calibrate any model on forward data and report sample count, horizon, uncertainty method, and market regime. Do not invent values merely to complete a candidate record.
probability_and_decision_semantics.states: ACCEPT means all setup, execution, payoff, and risk checks passed in the current mode. WAIT means a bounded confirmation is pending, with expiry and invalidation. REDUCE means an otherwise valid setup is resized using a tested integer contract rule; when one contract cannot be reduced, reject or abstain. REJECT means a defined rule failed. ABSTAIN means uncertainty, data, market, or execution conditions exceed the approved operating envelope. Keep the reason distinct.

runtime_safety.deterministic_decisions: Version and make entry, exit, position size, and risk decisions deterministic. An LLM may explain records and assist offline research; it cannot override limits, invent executable prices, alter live parameters, or issue discretionary orders.
runtime_safety.order_integrity: Use durable signal, intent, order, and fill identities. Retries and replays must not create duplicate positions. Reconcile actual fills, partial fills, active protection, cancellations, and late fills. Rejected or unknown protection blocks new entries and enters a documented emergency handling state.
runtime_safety.restart_and_kill: Persist the kill switch and lifecycle. After restart or disconnect, reconcile positions, orders, reservations, and account state before resuming entries. Unknown state blocks new entries. In automated modes, verify cancel/flatten results through approved routes. In manual prop mode, alert Frank urgently and record his actual resolution; never claim automatic flattening.
runtime_safety.boundaries: Test PAPER_AUTO has no real order route, PROP_MANUAL_ALERTS has no order or UI submission route, and LIVE_AUTO remains disabled. Do not store credentials in code, logs, or reports. Use no real-account credentials to qualify the paper path.

account_rules.profile: Build a versioned interface for firm, account product, purchase cohort, platform, stage, effective date, rule provenance, daily and trailing floors, open-PnL treatment, contract caps, scale rules, trade windows, evaluation targets, consistency, payouts, and permitted automation. Test rule boundaries at just below, exactly at, and just above the limit.
account_rules.selection: Frank's intended prop route is Apex through Tradovate, executed manually. Do not select a Topstep example or combine legacy and current Apex terms. Account-specific prop recommendations remain unconfigured until the exact product and applicable current rules are known. Independent paper work proceeds.
account_rules.manual_alert: Include strategy and signal IDs, contract, side, setup, detection/expiry, entry zone, stop, target, suggested whole-contract quantity, worst-case risk, current rule status, and invalidation. Record delivery, Frank's decision, actual entry and exit, actual protection, and any missed or stale alert. Keep autonomous paper, delayed-manual simulation, and actual prop results separate.

validation_and_promotion.development: Register hypotheses and all tested variants. Use chronological development and walk-forward windows; purge overlapping labels at boundaries; keep final protected out-of-sample data untouched until its planned release. Compare to simpler baselines, use feature ablations, and include executable costs in every deployable comparison. Track regime, session, long/short, strategy, parameter, latency, cost, and slippage sensitivity. Do not repeatedly select a winner on the final holdout.
validation_and_promotion.paper_start: A working simulated signal-to-ledger path, correct accounting, and essential failure checks permit paper observations. Do not require a profitable historical result before collecting actual paper data. Label synthetic replay separately.
validation_and_promotion.initial_review: Use the master's initial floor of at least 100 completed positions, 20 sessions, and four calendar weeks under fixed rules. This is a review floor, not proof of a 70 percent population win probability. Count complete positions, define breakeven treatment, and report sample and regime coverage.
validation_and_promotion.paper_to_manual_prop: Require observed net win rate at least 70 percent, positive mean net expectancy with a prespecified session-aware 95 percent lower confidence bound above zero, no hard-rule breach, acceptable execution and stress behavior, a selected exact prop rule profile, and an untouched forward segment. A 70 percent observed rate is not itself a 70 percent lower confidence bound. Keep strategy variants separate unless a pooled policy and test were specified in advance.
validation_and_promotion.stress: Simulate complete paths with the exact floor, daily stop, costs, and size rules. Include correlated loss blocks, adverse slippage, delayed or missed fills, fewer setups, and gaps. Report pass-before-breach, breach and unresolved fractions, drawdown, and time conditional on passing. Use the master's proposed 10000-path base and adverse stress tolerances as predeclared paper criteria; label them design tolerances rather than observed guarantees.
validation_and_promotion.manual_prop_to_live: Preserve Frank's two-funded-payout requirement, continued net-positive and rule-compliant results, the 70 percent objective unless he explicitly revises it, separate autonomous broker execution qualification, minimum size, and explicit personal-live activation. Prop alerts and human-entered orders do not prove autonomous broker reliability.

record_schema.common: Run ID, mode, strategy/config and code version, data source/version, account profile/version, instrument/contract, tick metadata, UTC exchange/receive/ decision timestamps, timezone/session, cost model, and outcome provenance.
record_schema.candidate: Signal/setup ID and strategy family; direction; known-at-decision H4/H1/M15/M5/M1 features; level and zone references with creation/confirmation time; regime, event, quote and spread status; entry zone and expiry; stop and target references; gross/net payoff estimate; assumed or calibrated probabilities with status; risk capacity, intended quantity, every limit result, final decision state, and explicit rejection or abstention reason. Optional research fields are nullable and cannot block the baseline merely because an experiment is absent.
record_schema.daily_report: Executed positions, skips by reason, net PnL and costs, observed win rate, mean net R, drawdown and headroom, rule and operational faults, and progress toward fixed evidence gates. Display source-engine benchmark, current-bot result, and user target as three separate labels.

implementation_work_order.step: Read the PDF and repository instructions. Inspect the checkout, preserve uncommitted work, confirm current startup and audit-reported bottlenecks, and write a short evidence-backed gap list. Do not commission another broad research report before connecting the paper path.
Add explicit PAPER_AUTO, PROP_MANUAL_ALERTS, and disabled LIVE_AUTO routing. Prove adapter isolation with a focused test or equivalent inspection.

Connect candidate, deterministic setup confirmation, risk approval, simulated order, fills, protective exit, and ledger. Demonstrate one qualifying synthetic sequence and one rule-rejected sequence end to end.

Formalize REVERSAL_R1 and CONTINUATION_C1 from the master using causal features, setup-specific tests, integer sizing, account capacity, session/event handling, and the existing safeguards. Fix uncovered failures in the same bounded implementation.

Run relevant existing tests plus focused cases for delayed pivots, future-bar leakage, duplicate/replayed orders, simultaneous risk reservations, floor ratchets, ambiguous bars, stale quotes, missing calendar, partial or rejected protection, restart recovery, and manual alert expiry. Report commands and results.

Run genuine full-session paper observation when accessible. If the market or feed is unavailable, leave an executable launch procedure and label replay results honestly. Then build the manual prop alert loop and exact-profile fixtures without connecting prop execution.

Use the research environment to stage and test optional features and strategy variants after the working path exists. A promising idea is not active until a versioned decision and forward validation support it.

response_contract.during_work: Give concise progress updates after meaningful findings or changes. Continue implementation within the authorized scope instead of stopping after a plan or asking Frank to reconfirm work he already requested.
response_contract.final_report: State what was changed with file references, what runs end to end, relevant tests and their outcomes, what remains unverified, and the next concrete paper observation step. Show source benchmark, measured bot performance, and target distinctly. Do not generate a 340-section essay, claim a 70 percent bot win rate without measured trades, or claim a live route is safe merely because the paper simulator works.
response_contract.first_action: Read Trading-bot-code-master.pdf and the existing checkout, identify the smallest missing link in the paper execution path, then implement and verify that link. Continue through the work order as far as the available project and data permit.
